issues.legal_issue: A delegation allowing the executive to lower a statutory maximum rent is valid when the legislation states its policy and provides guidance for exercising the delegated power.
material_facts: The legislation sought to improve peasants’ economic and social conditions and to protect tenants from excessive rent.
It set a maximum rent linked to the crop and the type of land.
It provided a process for fixing reasonable rent and specified factors for that determination, including local rental values, agricultural profits, crop prices, improvements, and land assessment.
It authorized the government to lower the maximum rent for particular areas or on another suitable basis, without prescribing a minimum rent.
The majority treated the policy expressed in the legislation and the factors governing reasonable rent as guidance for the government’s area-specific exercise of the power.
issues.conclusion: The delegation was not excessive; the provision conferring the power was valid, and the absence of a prescribed minimum rent did not alter that conclusion.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature may delegate subsidiary or ancillary powers but may not delegate its essential legislative function. It must state the legislative policy and principle and provide guidance for the delegate. Whether it has done so is assessed from the preamble and relevant provisions read together. The majority relied on Harishankar Bagla v. State of Madhya Pradesh and The Edward Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of Ajmer, and found that the tenant-protection policy and the factors specified for fixing reasonable rent adequately guided the delegated power.

rule.if: excessive_delegation_challenge and tenant_protection_policy_declared and crop_linked_rent_ceiling_set and reasonable_rent_factors_provided and area_specific_adjustment_power_conferred

predicates.excessive_delegation_challenge: The proceeding challenges a law on the ground that it delegates legislative power excessively.
predicates.tenant_protection_policy_declared: The legislature stated a policy of protecting tenants and improving their economic or social conditions.
predicates.crop_linked_rent_ceiling_set: The legislature itself set a maximum rent linked to the crop or other characteristics of the land.
predicates.reasonable_rent_factors_provided: The legislation specified factors for authorities to consider when determining reasonable rent.
predicates.area_specific_adjustment_power_conferred: The legislation authorized the government to adjust the maximum rent for particular areas.

issues.definition: When an excessive-delegation challenge concerns a law that declares a tenant-protection policy, sets a crop-linked ceiling, provides factors for determining reasonable rent, and authorizes area-specific adjustments, the rule treats the delegation as within permissible limits.

issues.legal_issue: An executive notification issued under a statute protected against a property-rights challenge cannot be invalidated on that ground merely because it exercises the authority conferred by the statute.
material_facts: The statute was protected by a constitutional provision that placed it in a protected schedule.
The challenged notification was issued under the statute’s delegated power to set a lower maximum rent.
The challengers argued that the notification infringed constitutional property rights.
issues.conclusion: The notification could not be challenged as infringing constitutional property rights because the statute and the power it conferred were protected.
issues.legal_principle: Where the statute is protected by the constitutional schedule, a notification issued through a valid exercise of power conferred by that statute cannot be treated as fresh legislation and challenged on the ground that it infringes the constitutional property-rights provision.

predicates.property_rights_challenge_to_notificatio: The proceeding challenges an executive notification on the ground that it violates constitutional property rights.
predicates.parent_statute_constitutionally_protecte: The statute authorizing the notification is constitutionally protected against that kind of challenge.
predicates.notification_issued_under_parent_statute: The executive issued the notification under authority conferred by the protected statute.

issues.definition: If a property-rights challenge targets a notification issued under a constitutionally protected statute, the notification is not invalid on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory power conferred on the government to adjust a maximum rent may be exercised more than once unless the legislation indicates a contrary intention.
material_facts: The government issued an initial notification under the statutory power and later issued another notification under the same power, superseding earlier notifications.
The challengers argued that the power had been exhausted by its first exercise and relied in part on the omission of wording expressly permitting repeated exercise.
The applicable general interpretation rule provided that a power conferred on the government could be exercised from time to time as occasion required.
The court found no contrary legislative intention and observed that agricultural rent may need adjustment as conditions change.
issues.conclusion: The power was not exhausted by its first exercise and could be exercised again as occasion required.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the provision of the applicable general clauses legislation under which a power conferred on a government may be exercised from time to time as occasion requires. It found no different intention in the statute and concluded that the power to modify the maximum rent was not intended to be exercised only once.

rule.if: repeat_exercise_challenge and government_adjustment_power_conferred and repeat_exercise_allowed_absent_contrary_intent and no_contrary_intention_shown

predicates.repeat_exercise_challenge: The proceeding challenges a later exercise of a government power on the ground that the power was exhausted by an earlier exercise.
predicates.government_adjustment_power_conferred: The legislation conferred on the government a power to adjust a statutory maximum.
predicates.repeat_exercise_allowed_absent_contrary_: The applicable general interpretation rule permits a government power to be exercised from time to time unless a different intention appears.
predicates.no_contrary_intention_shown: The legislation does not show an intention that the power may be exercised only once.

issues.definition: When a later exercise of a government adjustment power is challenged as exhausted, the power may be exercised repeatedly if the general rule permits repeated exercise and the legislation shows no contrary intention.
